tasks.short: Prepare sales contracts and order forms from agreed products, prices and terms.

steps.what: Collect agreed products, quantities, prices and customer details from the {CRM}.
Check product codes, availability and permitted prices in the {ERP}.
Populate contract and order templates stored in the {DOCS}.
Review drafts for customer commitments and departures from approved terms.
Approve commercial or legal exceptions within the relevant mandate.
Send approved documents to the customer for acceptance or signature.
Register accepted documents and transfer the order to the order desk.

tasks.design: Connect the {CRM} deal record to validation rules in the {ERP} and approved templates in the {DOCS}. A workflow in the {WORKFLOW} routes exceptions, requires approval before external issue through the {ESIGN}, and registers accepted orders without retyping.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agreed terms, price checks and templates were maintained separately. Exceptions made blanket automation unattractive.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing configuration and template tools cover standard cases. AI coding can reduce the effort of building validators and system connections.
tasks.still_hard: Customer clauses, conflicting commercial commitments and unreliable availability data need attention. Acceptance must match the exact issued document version.
tasks.human_edge: The representative recognises commitments that would damage trust or margin. Authorised approvers accept commercial and legal risk.

ambition.what: Same-day standard contract pack for repeat buyers

tasks.altitude: The week contains fewer document edits and more negotiation preparation. The representative can release standard packs within an agreed mandate; exception approval rights remain with authorised approvers.

reach.task: Resolve order-line validation failures before fulfilment.
reach.learn: Item codes, delivery constraints and order acceptance checks.
Margin calculations and the commercial approval matrix.

evidence.claim: Elfsquad links configuration and quoting to ERP and CRM, with human checks.
The ZARGES vendor case reports quote preparation falling from about 15 minutes to 90 seconds; contract preparation may differ.
Controlled templates, price rules and acceptance checks can handle standard contract packs without a model.

assumptions: The baseline is a mid-size European B2B seller using the {CRM}, {ERP} and document templates.
Shares are estimated task labour across the listed actors. Conditional approvals are averaged across cases.
Agreed terms can be captured in structured fields; missing fields become exceptions.
The document-heavy prior supports template automation, but does not imply that a model is needed.
GDPR applies to customer contacts and signatures. EU AI Act duties depend on the actual deployment; national rules vary.
unknowns: Which system connections and template features are licensed and accessible?
What proportion of contracts contains bespoke clauses?
Who can approve discounts, legal clauses and external issue?
research_questions: Can standard templates represent the most frequent contract variants?
Which validation failures account for most order-desk rework?
Can acceptance events identify the exact document version automatically?
new_work: Review missing terms and failed product or price checks.
Maintain templates, clause versions and approval thresholds.
Monitor duplicate orders and failed acceptance transfers.
Check recipients and final versions before external issue.

tasks.short: Choose and provide product samples and relevant catalogs to customers.

steps.what: Discuss the customer's intended use and sample needs.
Choose samples and catalog sections using product information in the {DOCS}.
Check sample availability and permitted quantities in the {ERP}.
Send the selected catalog to the customer through the {EMAIL}.
Request selected samples from the warehouse through the {EMAIL}.
Pick, pack and dispatch the requested physical samples.
Present samples and explain differences during the customer visit.
Record sample delivery, customer feedback and follow-up in the {CRM}.

tasks.design: Use a sample-request form in the {CRM} to check the {ERP}, send selected catalogs from the {DOCS}, and create warehouse requests in the {OPS_SYSTEM}. Delivery events update sample history automatically, while people select products, handle physical samples and discuss customer reactions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Physical samples and customer conversations dominated the task. Small requests were passed through a mailbox without a shared delivery record.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms, stock lookups and notifications can connect the administrative steps. A model adds little to this flow.
tasks.still_hard: Texture, finish, fit and practical suitability require physical evaluation. Sample stock may not be recorded as ordinary saleable stock.
tasks.human_edge: The representative notices hesitation and helps customers compare physical qualities that a catalog cannot convey.

ambition.what: A remote sample-request service for small repeat buyers

tasks.altitude: The representative spends less time chasing parcels and attaching catalogs. They gain visibility into sample follow-up, but no additional pricing or fulfilment approval rights.

reach.task: Run a structured comparison of competing sample options.
reach.learn: Demonstration techniques and questions that reveal practical suitability.

reach.task: Coordinate sample dispatch and resolve address or stock exceptions.
reach.learn: Warehouse request fields and delivery-status handling.

evidence.claim: Forms, stock checks and dispatch notifications can automate sample administration without replacing physical demonstrations.

assumptions: Catalogs are approved public materials and are sent in response to customer requests.
Physical handling and customer discussion dominate, consistent with the human-work prior.
Shares include warehouse labour associated with fulfilling sample requests.
GDPR applies to contact details and delivery addresses. National rules govern promotional communications; EU AI Act duties apply if AI is later added.
unknowns: Are sample items and quantities recorded in the {ERP} or {OPS_SYSTEM}?
Which sample requests require approval because of value or restricted products?
Can customers request samples remotely today?
Who maintains current catalogs and language variants?
research_questions: Can requested catalogs and sample dispatch use existing configuration?
Which sample requests most often fail because of stock or address problems?
Would small repeat buyers use a remote request form?
new_work: Maintain catalog versions and sample-request limits.
Handle missing stock, incorrect addresses and failed delivery events.
Capture customer feedback and choose the next follow-up action.

tasks.short: Track market changes, product innovations and competitor offerings to inform sales decisions.

steps.what: Read trade publications and competitor pages using a browser and the {DOCS}.
Ask customers and distributors about demand, alternatives and observed prices.
Update competitor comparisons and source notes in the {SPREADSHEET}.

loop.input: Approved source documents and manually captured market observations.
loop.output: A sourced comparison of products, prices and innovations, with uncertainty labels.
loop.check: Require a supporting passage for every claim; check dates, currencies, units and price conditions.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction per document, within a fixed document limit; failed rows go to review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Catalogs and trade articles express comparable facts in inconsistent prose and layouts.

steps.what: Compare observations with internal sales trends in the {ERP} and {BI}.
Assess which changes matter for assigned accounts and prepare recommendations.
Discuss recommendations and agree sales priorities with the sales manager.

tasks.design: A scheduled job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} collects permitted sources and detects changes, then a bounded extraction loop drafts a sourced comparison in the {DOCS}. The {BI} combines verified observations with sales data from the {ERP}; the representative interprets account implications and agrees team actions with the sales manager.
tasks.previous_blocker: Useful information was scattered across publications, catalogs and conversations. Comparing claims required reading inconsistent formats.
tasks.enabler_now: Scheduled retrieval and change detection are established techniques. Bounded extraction can turn prose into comparable fields with supporting passages.
tasks.still_hard: Competitor sales are often unavailable, and advertised prices may exclude discounts or delivery. Customer anecdotes can misrepresent wider demand.
tasks.human_edge: The representative tests weak signals against customer relationships and distinguishes a temporary promotion from a meaningful market shift.

ambition.what: Weekly account outreach priorities based on verified product and price changes

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from repeated browsing toward customer interviews and interpreting changes. The representative can choose account follow-up within the agreed sales priorities; pricing and assortment decisions still require their existing approvers.

reach.task: Translate demand signals into a revised sales forecast.
reach.learn: Forecast assumptions, segment weighting and uncertainty.

reach.task: Assess whether a product innovation changes customer suitability.
reach.learn: Specification comparison and evidence for product claims.

evidence.claim: Scheduled source collection, change alerts and sourced document summaries can support market monitoring.
Public competitor information cannot establish undisclosed sales volumes or negotiated prices.

assumptions: Source access is permitted; retrieval uses a fixed source list rather than autonomous browsing.
Customer conversations remain human and are captured manually; call recording is outside this design.
The baseline assigns 35% to conversations, below the meeting-heavy prior, because document comparison is a separate recurring activity.
Unverified observations remain labelled and cannot silently become verified facts.
GDPR applies to identifiable customer observations. EU AI Act duties and national communication rules depend on use.
unknowns: Which publications and competitor sources may be collected and retained?
Which product families and account segments matter most?
How are customer observations currently recorded?
Who can change sales priorities, prices and assortment?
research_questions: Which sources provide timely facts rather than repeated promotional claims?
Can extraction preserve price conditions and distinguish comparable products?
Which alerts would cause a concrete account action?
new_work: Review unsupported claims and ambiguous product matches.
Maintain source permissions, retrieval rules and comparison fields.
Remove stale prices and duplicate announcements.
Test market signals with customers before recommending changes.

tasks.short: Maintain sales records, prepare budgets and reports, and submit expense claims.

steps.what: Update sales activity, order status and next actions in the {CRM}.
Combine exports from the {CRM} and {ERP} in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Reconcile reporting totals and investigate mismatches in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Calculate a sales budget baseline using the {SPREADSHEET}.
Adjust budget assumptions for account changes, demand and planned activity.
Compile sales results and the budget into reporting templates in the {DOCS}.
Review submitted assumptions and approve the sales budget.
Attach receipts, enter business purpose and submit claims in the {EXPENSE}.
Check expense evidence and approve or return the claim.

tasks.design: Scheduled connections on the {DATA_PLATFORM} reconcile the {CRM} and {ERP}, feed a {BI} report, and generate budget submissions in the {DOCS}. Configure the {EXPENSE} for transaction import, required evidence and policy checks, while people supply business purpose, set forecast assumptions and approve budgets or claims.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sales and finance used different definitions, exports and reporting periods. Expense paperwork formed a separate administrative queue.
tasks.enabler_now: Configuration, scheduled data joins and template generation already cover most mechanics. AI coding can reduce the effort of implementing mappings and reconciliation checks.
tasks.still_hard: Returns, credits, revenue timing and account ownership can distort totals. Forecast assumptions and expense legitimacy remain human judgements.
tasks.human_edge: The representative explains why an account will grow or shrink and supplies honest business context that transaction records cannot establish.

ambition.what: Weekly territory forecast updates before the monthly budget review

tasks.altitude: The representative spends less time assembling reports and more time testing account assumptions. They gain faster scenario preparation and can propose territory changes; budget and reimbursement approval rights remain with their approvers.

reach.task: Review territory forecast changes and allocate selling effort.
reach.learn: Forecast calibration, capacity constraints and scenario comparison.

reach.task: Resolve discrepancies between booked orders, returns and invoiced sales.
reach.learn: Order status, credit notes and sales-period definitions.

evidence.claim: Sales reporting, record synchronisation and expense policy checks generally use deterministic rules.
The cited Dutch works-council rule covers arrangements for observing employee behaviour or performance.

assumptions: The {CRM}, {ERP} and {EXPENSE} are used today; the {SPREADSHEET} bridges reporting definitions.
Shares average recurring administration and less frequent budget work, including associated approval labour.
The high automation prior fits report assembly, but forecast assumptions and business-purpose entry retain human work.
GDPR applies to activity records and expenses. Any seller-monitoring change requires assessment of national consultation rules.
In the Netherlands, covered monitoring arrangements require works council consent; national rules vary elsewhere.
EU AI Act duties apply if model features are added. This design needs no model.
Build ranges estimate working effort; consultation and access waiting time can extend elapsed delivery.
unknowns: How are booked sales, invoiced sales, returns and credits defined?
Are reliable account identifiers shared across the {CRM} and {ERP}?
Does the {EXPENSE} support transaction imports and configurable policy checks?
Would the change introduce employee monitoring or alter an existing arrangement?
Which employee representatives and approval bodies must be consulted?
research_questions: Can existing reporting configuration replace manual exports?
Which reconciliation rules catch material errors without excessive false alarms?
Can aggregate territory reporting meet the need without additional individual activity tracking?
new_work: Resolve reconciliation exceptions and failed data refreshes.
Maintain metric definitions, account mappings and reporting periods.
Review forecast assumptions against subsequent outcomes.
Maintain expense rules and handle missing evidence.
Manage access, retention and any required employee consultation.

role.altitude: The representative's week shifts toward customer conversations, account judgement and commercial preparation. Faster records and evidence support decisions within their mandate; broader pricing, contract and budget rights require explicit delegation.
reach: Order clerk: prevent order and sample fulfilment exceptions before handoff.
Sales manager: prepare account forecasts and evaluate commercial scenarios.
Product demonstrator: structure physical product comparisons around customer use.
skills_to_grow: Structured capture of agreed terms and customer requirements.
Reading sourced market comparisons and testing uncertain claims.
Handling workflow exceptions and maintaining accurate records.
role.ambitious_version: Run a territory service that combines same-day standard contract packs, remote sample requests and weekly account priorities from verified market changes, while preserving human product advice and commercial approval.

job.title: Sales Representatives, Wholesale and Manufacturing, Except Technical and Scientific Products
